trigger: Outgoing internal IT coordinator leaving in three weeks

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Olivia Hart, Sam from Harbourline IT. Before we get into options, are you still the practice manager at Wattle Street Legal in Hawthorn?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: Yes. We're thirty-seven people, mostly solicitors, paralegals and admin. I booked the call because our internal IT coordinator resigned and leaves in three weeks.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: What does that coordinator currently hold in their head that worries you most?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: Almost everything. They know the document system quirks, which partners have unusual setups, how court filing certificates work, and which laptops are overdue for replacement. Some of it's written down, but not enough.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: How are support requests handled now when solicitors are under deadline pressure?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: People walk to the coordinator or message me. It works because they are here, but it's not scalable. Family law deadlines are emotional, and a locked account before a filing deadline becomes my problem fast.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Who needs to approve a managed services agreement before the coordinator leaves?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: The principal solicitor and I can approve if the numbers are sensible. Finance will check cash flow, but this is an operational risk we can't leave open.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: What must be stable in the first month for you to feel the transition worked?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: Helpdesk coverage, leavers and joiners, backups, certificates for court systems, and someone documenting our Microsoft 365 admin settings. I also need staff to know who to call on day one.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: What is your current risk around cyber insurance or client confidentiality questionnaires?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: Insurers asked about MFA and backups last year. We answered, but it was informal. The principal wants something more defensible this year, especially because we handle sensitive family matters.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: For Wattle Street Legal, the managed service would be about $132 per seat per month, with a transition project focused on documentation, identity, backups and support handover.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: I am nervous about changing provider while our internal IT coordinator is leaving. If the handover is clumsy, everyone will blame me for breaking something that mostly works.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: That is completely reasonable. I would not suggest a big-bang change. We would run a two-week shadow handover with your coordinator, document the critical systems first and only then switch the helpdesk number. I will send the transition plan and fixed onboarding quote by Tuesday.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: A shadow handover would calm people down. The principal will ask whether you can handle after-hours work, because file migrations during business hours aren't acceptable.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: I will include the leaver checklist and after-hours file migration window. We can also give staff a simple support card so they know the new process before the coordinator leaves.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: Good. The monthly fee isn't the cheapest option, but the timing means I care more about a controlled handover than saving a few dollars per seat.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Can we review the plan Tuesday 8 September at 10am with you and the principal solicitor? If that works, we can start the discovery checklist the next morning.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: Yes, Tuesday 8 September at 10am works. Send the invite and the plan before close of business Monday if you can.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: I'd also like to interview your coordinator before they leave, not just collect passwords. The unwritten history is often where the real transition risk lives.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: Yes, please. They are helpful and will share what they know, but I need someone to ask the right questions while they are still here.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: We will prioritise court-system certificates, document access, admin rights and backup restore evidence before any cosmetic tidy-up. The goal is continuity first, then maturity.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: That order makes sense. Staff will forgive a slightly clunky portal before they forgive being unable to file documents or open matters.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: For communication, we can draft a simple internal note from you explaining the support change, the reason for it and exactly what staff should do from the first day.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: That would save me time. People get nervous when support changes, especially the partners who have had the same habits for years.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: We can start the handover with a short risk register as well, so you can show the principal what is critical, what is inconvenient and what can wait until after the coordinator leaves.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: That will make the approval conversation cleaner. The principal is practical, but she hates open-ended projects with no sense of priority.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Done. I will send the invite now, then the transition plan and fixed quote by Monday afternoon.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Olivia Hart
turns.text: Thanks Sam. This feels practical, which is what I needed.
